definitions.explanation: A small neighborhood shop selling cheap sweets and snacks ({駄菓子|だがし}) and simple toys to children, typically for ten or twenty yen an item.

examples.japanese: {駄菓子屋|だがしや}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{行|い}く→行く：00119_iku⟧。
examples.english: To go to the candy shop.

examples.japanese: ⟦{子供|こども}→子供：00554_kodomo⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦ころ→〜ころ：03091_koro⟧、⟦{毎日|まいにち}→毎日：00729_mainichi⟧{駄菓子屋|だがしや}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{通|かよ}った→通う：01217_kayou⟧。
examples.english: As a kid, I went to the candy shop every day.

examples.japanese: ⟦{昔|むかし}ながら→昔ながら：26817_mukashinagara⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{駄菓子屋|だがしや}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{減|へ}った→減る：01985_heru⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧、⟦{最近|さいきん}→最近：00881_saikin⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{大人|おとな}→大人：02856_otona⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{懐|なつ}かしがって⟦{訪|おとず}れる→訪れる：07678_otozureru⟧こと⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{多|おお}い→多い：01127_ooi⟧。
examples.english: Old-style candy shops have become rare, but these days many adults visit them out of nostalgia.

notes:
⟦{駄菓子|だがし}→駄菓子：14736_dagashi⟧ (cheap sweets) + ⟦{屋|や}→〜屋：03096_ya⟧ (shop). For many Japanese the {駄菓子屋|だがしや} is a symbol of the Showa-era childhood: after school, children gathered there with a coin or two, chose sweets, and played. Few remain today, but the word carries strong nostalgia.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {駄菓子屋|だがしや}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦おばあちゃん→おばあちゃん：10968_obaachan⟧: the old woman who runs the candy shop
- ⟦{町|まち}→町：00613_machi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{駄菓子屋|だがしや}: the neighborhood candy shop
- {駄菓子屋|だがしや}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{買|か}い{食|ぐ}い→買い食い：16976_kaigui⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to buy and eat snacks at the candy shop
